probes.question: Archimedes began with a regular polygon of how many sides?
True or false: Archimedes drew his polygons both inside and outside a circle.

image.alt: A hexagon drawn inside and outside a circle, then a 12-sided polygon, hugging the circle ever more closely

body.question: Archimedes drew a regular hexagon inside and outside a circle, then kept doubling the number of sides. How many sides did his last polygon have?
body.reveal: Archimedes computed upper and lower bounds of π by drawing a regular hexagon inside and outside a circle, and successively doubling the number of sides until he reached a 96-sided regular polygon.
